stem: The device used for producing current is called ______.
solution: A generator (dynamo) converts mechanical energy into electrical energy and is the device used for producing (generating) electric current. A voltmeter measures potential difference, an ammeter measures current, and a galvanometer detects small currents.

stem: If a ray of light passes from a denser medium to a rarer medium in a straight line, the angle of incidence must be ______.
solution: When the angle of incidence is \(0^\circ\) the ray travels along the normal, so it does not bend and passes straight through, irrespective of the two media. Hence the angle of incidence must be \(0^\circ\).

stem: The power of a convex lens of focal length 20 cm is ______.
solution: Power \(P = \dfrac{1}{f(\text{in metre})} = \dfrac{1}{0.20} = +5.0\,D\). A convex (converging) lens has positive power.

stem: Good conductor of electricity is ______.
solution: Among the given non-metals, graphite is the only good conductor of electricity because of the free (delocalised) electrons in its layered structure. Bromine, iodine and sulphur are non-conductors of electricity.

stem: The height of medium earth orbit above the surface of the earth is:
solution: The Medium Earth Orbit (MEO) lies roughly between 2,000 km and 35,780 km above the earth's surface, so 25,000 km falls within this range. (Low earth orbit is about 180-2,000 km.)

stem: Find the odd man out: Loudspeaker, Microphone, Electric motor, Magnet.
solution: Magnet is the odd one out. A loudspeaker, a microphone and an electric motor are devices that work on the interaction between electric current and magnetism (the magnetic effect of electric current), whereas a magnet is a simple component and not a device that operates on electric current.

stem: Complete the co-relation: \(CuI_2\) : Brown :: \(AgCl\) : ______.
solution: White. Just as copper(II) iodide \(CuI_2\) is brown in colour, silver chloride \(AgCl\) is a white coloured compound (it is obtained as a white precipitate).

stem: Match the pair. Group 'A' (Substance): Air. Group 'B' (Refractive index): (a) 1.33, (b) 1.46, (c) 1.0003.
solution: Air matches with (c) 1.0003. The refractive index of air is very close to 1 (about 1.0003). (1.33 is the refractive index of water and 1.46 is that of fused quartz.)

stem: State True or False: "Wavelength of red light is close to 700 nm."
solution: True. Red light lies at the long-wavelength end of the visible spectrum, with a wavelength of about 700 nm.

stem: Write the name of the small satellite made by a group of students from COEP (College of Engineering, Pune) sent to space through ISRO in 2016.
solution: Swayam. It is a small (pico) satellite built by students of the College of Engineering, Pune (COEP) and launched by ISRO in 2016 (on 22 June 2016, aboard PSLV-C34).

stem: Give a scientific reason: For electric power transmission, copper or aluminium wire is used.
solution: Copper and aluminium have very low electrical resistivity, i.e. they are excellent conductors of electricity, so the power lost as heat (\(I^2R\)) in the transmission wires is minimum. They are also highly ductile (can be drawn into long thin wires), fairly cheap and abundantly available. Therefore copper or aluminium wire is used for electric power transmission.

stem: Give a scientific reason: Lemon or tamarind is used for cleaning copper vessels turned greenish.
solution: On exposure to moist air, copper slowly reacts with carbon dioxide and moisture to form a green layer of basic copper carbonate \(CuCO_3 \cdot Cu(OH)_2\) on its surface (corrosion). Lemon and tamarind contain citric and tartaric acids; these mild acids react with and dissolve this green basic-carbonate layer, so the copper vessel becomes clean and shiny again.

stem: Give a scientific reason: Elements belonging to the same group have the same valency.
solution: The valency of an element is decided by the number of valence electrons (electrons in the outermost shell). All elements in the same group of the periodic table have the same number of valence electrons, and hence the same combining capacity. Therefore elements belonging to the same group have the same valency.

stem: How do we feel about air in each of the following conditions? (a) Relative humidity is more than 60%. (b) Relative humidity is less than 60%.
solution: (a) When the relative humidity is more than 60%, the air is very moist/humid. Sweat on our body does not evaporate easily, so we feel sultry, sticky and uncomfortable. (b) When the relative humidity is less than 60%, the air is dry. Sweat evaporates readily, carrying away body heat, so we feel dry and comfortable (cool).

stem: Complete the following reaction: \(C_{12}H_{22}O_{11} \xrightarrow{\text{heat}}\) ______ + ______.
solution: \(C_{12}H_{22}O_{11} \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 12C + 11H_2O\). On strong heating, sucrose (sugar) undergoes thermal decomposition (dehydration) to give carbon (a black residue) and water vapour.

subtopic: Free Fall and Acceleration due to Gravity
stem: Distinguish between Mass and Weight.
solution:
| Mass | Weight |
|---|---|
| It is the quantity of matter contained in a body. | It is the force with which the earth attracts the body. |
| It is a scalar quantity. | It is a vector quantity (directed towards the earth's centre). |
| SI unit is the kilogram (kg). | SI unit is the newton (N). |
| It remains constant everywhere. | It changes with place because it depends on \(g\) (\(W = mg\)). |
| Measured with a beam (physical) balance. | Measured with a spring balance. |

stem: Define periods and groups of the modern periodic table.
solution: Periods: The horizontal rows in the modern periodic table are called periods. There are 7 periods; the period number of an element equals the number of electron shells in its atom. Groups: The vertical columns in the modern periodic table are called groups. There are 18 groups; elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons and therefore similar chemical properties.

stem: Calculate the escape velocity on the surface of the moon, given the mass and radius of the moon to be \(7.34 \times 10^{22}\) kg and \(1.74 \times 10^{6}\) m respectively. (Given: \(G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}\,Nm^2/kg^2\)).
solution: Escape velocity \(v_{esc} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 7.34 \times 10^{22}}{1.74 \times 10^{6}}}\). The numerator \(= 9.79 \times 10^{12}\); dividing by \(1.74 \times 10^{6}\) gives \(5.63 \times 10^{6}\). Taking the square root, \(v_{esc} \approx 2.37 \times 10^{3}\,m/s \approx 2.37\,km/s\).

context: An element has its electron configuration as 2, 8, 1. Now answer the following questions:
stem: What is the atomic number of this element?
solution: Atomic number = total number of electrons \(= 2 + 8 + 1 = 11\). (The element is sodium, Na.)

context: An element has its electron configuration as 2, 8, 1. Now answer the following questions:
stem: What is the group of this element?
solution: The atom has 1 electron in its outermost shell (1 valence electron), so the element belongs to Group 1 of the modern periodic table.

context: An element has its electron configuration as 2, 8, 1. Now answer the following questions:
stem: To which period does the element belong?
solution: The atom has 3 electron shells (2, 8, 1), so the element belongs to Period 3 of the modern periodic table.

stem: Observe the figure and name the ray AB, ray CD and ray GH (light passing through a rectangular glass slab).
solution: Ray AB - incident ray (falling on the glass slab from air). Ray CD - refracted ray (travelling inside the glass, bent towards the normal). Ray GH - emergent ray (leaving the slab into air, parallel to the incident ray AB but laterally displaced).
figureNote: Ray diagram of light refracting through a rectangular glass slab (air-glass-air), with rays A-B-N, C-D, M-G-H marked and angles i, r, i1, e; p-07

stem: Why is NaCl an ionic compound?
solution: Sodium (a metal) has 1 electron in its outermost shell and chlorine (a non-metal) has 7. Sodium loses its 1 valence electron to form \(Na^+\) and chlorine gains that electron to form \(Cl^-\). The oppositely charged ions are held together by a strong electrostatic force of attraction (an ionic/electrovalent bond). Since NaCl is formed by transfer of electrons and is made up of ions, it is an ionic compound.

stem: State any two properties of ionic compounds.
solution: Any two: (1) They are hard crystalline solids with high melting and boiling points. (2) They are generally soluble in water but insoluble in organic solvents. (3) They do not conduct electricity in the solid state but conduct in the molten or aqueous (dissolved) state.

stem: Identify the physical and chemical changes from the following phenomena: (a) Transformation of ice into water. (b) Ripening of fruit. (c) Milk turned into curd. (d) Evaporation of water. (e) Digestion of food in the stomach. (f) Iron filings get attracted towards the magnet.
solution: (a) Transformation of ice into water - physical change. (b) Ripening of fruit - chemical change. (c) Milk turning into curd - chemical change. (d) Evaporation of water - physical change. (e) Digestion of food in the stomach - chemical change. (f) Iron filings getting attracted towards a magnet - physical change.

context: Observe the figure titled 'Specific heat capacity of metals' (identical balls of iron, copper and lead, heated to the same temperature, placed on a layer of wax) and answer the following:
stem: Which element has maximum specific heat capacity? Justify.
solution: Iron has the maximum specific heat capacity. Heated to the same temperature, the iron ball releases the most heat while cooling, so it melts the most wax and sinks deepest into the wax layer. (Specific heat of iron \(\approx 0.46\,J/g\,^\circ C\), the highest among the three.)
figureNote: Figure 'Specific heat capacity of metals': iron, copper and lead balls sunk to different depths in a wax layer; p-09

context: Observe the figure titled 'Specific heat capacity of metals' (identical balls of iron, copper and lead, heated to the same temperature, placed on a layer of wax) and answer the following:
stem: Which element has minimum specific heat capacity? Justify.
solution: Lead has the minimum specific heat capacity. The lead ball melts the least wax and sinks the least, showing that it gives out the least heat for the same fall in temperature. (Specific heat of lead \(\approx 0.13\,J/g\,^\circ C\), the lowest among the three.)

context: Observe the figure titled 'Specific heat capacity of metals' (identical balls of iron, copper and lead, heated to the same temperature, placed on a layer of wax) and answer the following:
stem: Define specific heat of an object.
solution: The specific heat capacity of a substance is the quantity of heat required to raise the temperature of unit mass (1 kg) of the substance by \(1^\circ C\) (or 1 K). Its SI unit is \(J/kg\,^\circ C\) (or \(J/kg\,K\)).

stem: Identify figures A, B and C and give their uses.
solution: A - Electric fuse (cartridge fuse): a safety device containing a thin wire of low melting point that melts and breaks the circuit when the current exceeds a safe value, protecting appliances from overload or short circuit. B - MCB (Miniature Circuit Breaker): an automatic switch that trips (breaks the circuit) on overload or short circuit and can be reset; used for circuit protection in place of a fuse. C - Galvanometer: a sensitive instrument used to detect and measure very small electric currents (and their direction) in a circuit.

stem: Complete the following flow chart of the classification of hydrocarbons by filling in the blank boxes (Hydrocarbons branch into 'Saturated' and a blank; the saturated branch leads to a blank type, general formula \(C_nH_{2n+2}\) and a blank example; the unsaturated branch leads to 'Alkene' and a blank type, with formulae and examples).
solution: Hydrocarbons are classified as Saturated and Unsaturated. Saturated hydrocarbons -> Alkanes -> general formula \(C_nH_{2n+2}\) -> Ex.: Methane \(CH_4\). Unsaturated hydrocarbons -> Alkenes and Alkynes. Alkene -> general formula \(C_nH_{2n}\) -> Ex.: Ethene. Alkyne -> general formula \(C_nH_{2n-2}\) -> Ex.: Ethyne (acetylene). Filled blanks: right top box = 'Unsaturated'; box under 'Saturated' = 'Alkane'; the blank formula box under 'Alkene' = \(C_nH_{2n}\); the second unsaturated type box = 'Alkyne'; example under the alkane branch = Methane; example under the alkyne branch = Ethyne.

stem: Name the defect of vision represented in the above figure.
solution: The defect of vision shown is Myopia (near-sightedness / short-sightedness). In this defect the image of a distant object is formed in front of the retina instead of on it.
figureNote: Eye diagram: parallel rays from a distant object focused in front of the retina (myopic eye); p-11

subtopic: Human Eye and Defects of Vision
context: Observe the figure (parallel rays from a distant object are converged by the eye to a focus in front of the retina) and answer the following questions:
stem: State the reasons for this defect.
solution: Myopia is caused by: (i) excessive curvature (bulging) of the eye lens, which increases its converging power, and/or (ii) elongation of the eyeball, which increases the distance between the eye lens and the retina. Because of either cause, the far point comes closer and the image of a distant object is formed in front of the retina.

subtopic: Human Eye and Defects of Vision
context: Observe the figure (parallel rays from a distant object are converged by the eye to a focus in front of the retina) and answer the following questions:
stem: How is it corrected?
solution: Myopia is corrected by using spectacles fitted with a concave (diverging) lens of suitable focal length/power. The concave lens diverges the incoming parallel rays before they enter the eye, so that the eye lens then focuses them exactly on the retina.

subtopic: Human Eye and Defects of Vision
context: Observe the figure (parallel rays from a distant object are converged by the eye to a focus in front of the retina) and answer the following questions:
stem: Draw the diagram to show the correction of this defect.
solution: Diagram (description): Parallel rays from a distant object first pass through a concave (diverging) lens placed in front of the eye. The lens diverges the rays; these diverged rays then enter the eye and are converged by the eye lens to form a clear, sharp image on the retina. Thus the concave lens shifts the focus from in front of the retina onto the retina.
